_worked_example: INTERRUPT. GDD §19.5's first of three. Second rung of the soft-cap telegraph. It interrupts because a reporter on the phone is a person waiting, and because by this point the clock is close enough that the player should hear it stop being ambient. Both options cost something real and neither is the wise one.

tr.title: Yorum istiyorlar
tr.body:
Muhabir kibar. Yıl sonu derlemesi için birkaç satır istiyor. O yıl kurulanlardan ayakta kalan birkaç şirketten birisin ve onun için bu bir hikâye.

Bir rakam verirsen yazıya girersin. Susarsan da girersin, sadece başka bir cümleyle.

en.title: They want a comment
en.body:
The reporter is polite. They want a few lines for the year-end round-up. You're one of the few companies still standing from that year, and to them that's a story.

Give them a number and you're in the piece. Say nothing and you're in it anyway, under a different sentence.

_revision_2026_09: Both rows were pure gains while the note said both cost something. A number buys brand and costs reputation (a small number, in print); silence buys reputation and costs brand.
